plan.notes: Source: Rensselaer Catalog 2023-2024 [Archived Catalog], official RPI catalog, 'Program: Computer Science' — the 128-credit-hour B.S. curriculum leading to the B.S. degree in computer science. Transcribed manually from the official term-by-term template on 2026-09-30; term subtotals verified 16+16+16+16+16+16+16+16 = 128. CATALOG-YEAR CAVEAT: the live catalog is 2025-2026, but its CS program page URL was not indexed/locatable through search, so this plan uses the newest archived edition with a complete official term-by-term sequence (2023-2024); its track-based template matches the current curriculum era (the four 4000-level tracks). Degree confirmed as B.S. in Computer Science (catalog title 'Program: Computer Science'). RPI 'Arch' model: juniors take the summer semester on campus plus one of fall/spring on campus (the other semester is the 'away' semester) — the template shows 'The Arch Summer Semester' and 'Fall OR Spring' for Year 3. The official template does not publish per-course prerequisites, so prereq arrays are left empty rather than inferred. Catalog footnote caveats: (1) students with sufficient CS background may skip CSCI 1100 and replace it with 4 credits of other 2000-level-or-higher CSCI courses; (2) students with no prior MATH 1010 experience should take BIOL 1010 + BIOL 1015/1016 in the fall of Year 1 instead of PHYS 1100; (3) no credit for both CSCI 2200 and MATH 2800; (4) CSCI 2500 may be replaced by ECSE 2660 (take only one); (5) track courses pending instructor availability. Track system: after the 1000/2000-level core, students focus on one of four tracks — (a) Theory and Algorithms, (b) Systems and Software, (c) Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Data Science, (d) Vision, Graphics, Robotics, and Visualization — each requiring eight courses totaling at least 30 credits (missing credits from 3-credit courses made up as free electives); the template's six 'Computer Science 4000-level Track Course' slots plus free electives cover this. Mathematics Option I/II requirements depend on the chosen track (Theory/AI tracks: MATH 2010 and a 4000-level MATH/MATP; Systems track: Option I from MATH 2010/4030/4100/4140/MATP 4600, Option II 2000+ MATH/MATP; Vision track: MATH 2010 and 2000+ MATH/MATP). Science Option: one or more courses totaling 4 credits from astronomy, biology, chemistry, earth and environmental science, or physics; ERTH 1030 excluded; P/NC and reading/independent study courses cannot be used. Students choose either BIOL 1015 or BIOL 1016 for the Year-1 biology lab. Track requirements in full: Theory and Algorithms — Math Opt I must be MATH 2010, Math Opt II a 4000-level MATH/MATP; CSCI 4000 requirements: one of CSCI 4020 / CSCI 496X Theory of Computation, one of CSCI 4210/4320/4430; depth electives: two of CSCI 4030/4040/4100/4230/4250/4260/4510/4560; breadth: one 4000-level MATH/MATP, one 4000-level CSCI or UCC-approved non-CSCI 4000-level. Systems and Software — Math Opt I from MATH 2010/4030/4100/4140/MATP 4600, Math Opt II 2000+ MATH/MATP; CSCI 4000 requirements: CSCI 4210 and CSCI 4430; depth: two of CSCI 4220/4310/4320/4380/4440/4450/4460/4470/4500; breadth: two 4000-level CSCI or UCC-approved non-CSCI. AI/ML/Data Science — Math Opt I must be MATH 2010, Math Opt II a 4000-level MATH/MATP; CSCI 4000 requirements: one of CSCI 4100/4150/4350/4390, one of CSCI 4210/4320/4380; depth: two of CSCI 4100/4150/4270/4380/4390; breadth: one from CSCI 4100/4150/4210/4270/4320/4380/4340/4350/4370/4390 or any 4000-level MATH/MATP, one 4000-level CSCI or UCC-approved non-CSCI. Vision/Graphics/Robotics/Visualization — Math Opt I must be MATH 2010, Math Opt II 2000+ MATH/MATP; CSCI 4000 requirements: two of CSCI 4020/4210/4430; depth: two of CSCI 4270/4320/4480/4530/4550/4560; breadth: two 4000-level CSCI or UCC-approved non-CSCI. Transfer credit policy: majors must take five of their eight named required CSCI courses at RPI, with at least 32 required CSCI credits earned at RPI.
